slides.heading: Longest Balanced Substring
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Strings
slides.narration: Let's solve Longest Balanced Substring, a very hard strings problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Length of the longest balanced-parentheses substring.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Length of the longest balanced-parentheses substring. Two counting passes.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Count opens and closes left to right, then right to left, resetting when the balance breaks.
slides.narration: Count opens and closes left to right, then right to left, resetting when the balance breaks.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Stack of indices → O(n), O(n) space
slides.narration: Checking every substring is cubic. A stack of indices is linear; two counting scans in opposite directions are linear with constant space.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Left to right, equal counts give a candidate
slides.narration: Step by step. First, left to right, equal counts give a candidate. Second, reset when closes exceed opens. Third, repeat right to left.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Find the longest balanced substring
slides.narration: Find the longest balanced substring of parentheses.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Left-to-right scan
slides.narration: Scan left to right counting opens and closes. Equal counts give a candidate; more closes means reset.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Answer: 8
slides.narration: A second scan from the right catches cases with surplus opens. The answer is 8.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Scan counts opens and closes, records two times closes when equal, and resets when closes exceed opens; reverse mode swaps the roles.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: One direction alone misses cases like extra opens.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Count opens and closes left to right, then right to left, resetting when the balance breaks.
slides.narration: To recap Longest Balanced Substring: Count opens and closes left to right, then right to left, resetting when the balance breaks. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
